title: HF396 (2023-2024 Regular): Safe storage of firearms and ammunition required, violation of safe storage statute included as ineligibility to possess firearm, locking device required to be included in each firearm transfer, and criminal penalties imposed.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (1st Engrossment, 2023-02-09; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/HF/396/versions/1/)
provenance.note: Other: 1st Engrossment, 2023-02-09. The bill has no passage vote on file. Section 1 adds a violation of the new storage law to the list of offences that make a person ineligible to possess firearms for three years (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1, clause (11)); its new words are quoted (added at the bill-table step, 2026-11-19); Section 4 repeals the older negligent-storage law, section 609.666. Subd. 3(d) (felony, five years or $25,000, for an unsecured firearm used in a violent felony) is not quoted for length.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1): (11) a person who has been convicted of the following offenses at the gross misdemeanor level, unless three years have elapsed since the date of conviction and, during that time, the person has not been convicted of any other violation of these sections: ... 609.749 (harassment or stalking); or 624.7163 (firearm and ammunition storage requirements).
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 1): (a) The owner of a firearm must take reasonable action to secure the firearm when it is not carried or under the control of the owner or an authorized user. For this purpose, reasonable action requires a firearm to be stored unloaded with a locking device and separately from its ammunition or as provided for in paragraph (b).
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 1): (b) Peace officers and persons authorized to carry pistols under section 624.714 who store a loaded, holstered pistol in a quick-access safe have taken reasonable action to secure the firearm for purposes of this section.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 2): No person shall transfer a firearm to another person without an appropriate locking device unless the transferee provides proof of ownership of a locking device capable of storing the firearm in compliance with subdivision 1. The transferee must own a sufficient number of locking devices to secure each firearm the transferee owns.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 3): (a) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a misdemeanor.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 3): (b) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if a firearm that belongs to the person is not secured and is either loaded or in the immediate area of the unsecured firearm's ammunition.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 3): (c) A person who violates subdivision 1 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to 18 months in prison or a fine of up to $5,000, or both, if a loaded, unsecured firearm that belongs to the person is accessed by a child or a person prohibited from possessing firearms under section 624.713, subdivision 1.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 3): (e) A person who violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a misdemeanor.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7163, subd. 4): Subdivision 3, paragraphs (a) to (d), do not apply if access to the firearm was obtained as a result of an unlawful entry into a structure where the firearm is located.
